textBlocks.text: What happens if we do not repeat measurements and take averages in an experiment?
A more reliable / B errors may affect accuracy / C total weight increases / D automatically valid
You notice that the plants near the window grow faster than those far from the window.
You start to wonder why the plants near the window grow faster?
You think, maybe more sunlight allows plants to grow faster.
You decide to place two identical plants, one near the window and one inside the room, giving both the same water and fertilizer, and record their heights each week.

variablesHint.independent: location / amount of light (near window vs inside room)

textBlocks.text: You organize the weekly plant heights into a table and plot a growth curve.
You find that the plant near the window grows noticeably taller, so you make a conclusion based on the data.
Does the Amount of Screen Time Affect Eye Strain?
Main steps: Identify a problem, form a hypothesis, design and carry out an experiment, collect and analyse data, and draw a conclusion.
Independent variable: changed deliberately. Dependent variable: measured or observed.

draftQuestions.plan: Convert: which stage is 'notice plants near window grow faster' → Observation
Convert: placing two plants / same water & fertilizer / record heights → Designing and performing an experiment
Convert: table + growth curve → Data processing and analysis
Convert: taller plant + conclude from data → Drawing a conclusion (or order-of-steps item)
Screen time scenario — identify independent variable
Screen time scenario — identify dependent variable
Plant scenario — controlled variable (water / fertilizer / identical plants) OR definition of IV/DV
Keep ready MCQ on repeating measurements. Better fit Measurement (1.5); optional spare for 1.1 if you want a 'fair test / reliability' item. Not counted in 1.1×5 / 1.2×5 unless you say so.
